Adam Withrow

Unity candidate for United States Senator, Colorado · Challenger

Educator, builder and mountain guide (self-described); has also worked as a ranch hand, CNA, cook, contractor and detention officer

Adam Withrow is the Unity Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Colorado on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot. He describes himself as a working-class candidate, not a politician, and has worked as a ranch hand, certified nursing assistant, cook, contractor and detention officer. He is running against Democratic incumbent John Hickenlooper, Republican Mark Baisley, and three other minor-party candidates.

Where Withrow stands

Wages / Cost of living
Proposes a federal living wage tied to the Consumer Price Index so wages rise with prices. He would phase it in by industry based on gross receipts and profitability. He calls raising wages his first priority.
Foreign policy
Calls for a unilateral U.S. declaration of peace and an end to what he calls a global military empire, while keeping national self-defense. Opposes U.S. involvement in 'wars of choice.'
Climate / energy
Says fossil fuels are finite and 'obsolete' as a basis for future building, while acknowledging continued use. Supports starting a transition to newer energy technology now.
Health care
Supports redesigning the health care system to cover everyone. Argues that 'healthcare for all' would cost less than half of the defense budget.
Campaign finance / Lobbying
Says lobbyist and donor money amounts to 'legal bribery.' Says he does not seek big donors and is not beholden to either major party.
Direct democracy / Senate votes
Proposes putting each Senate vote to Colorado voters first and casting his vote the way they decide.
Technology / AI
Supports working toward moving data centers into orbit. Lists energy, water and AI among his top concerns.
